# Derivation 3.4A — Stationary source-to-field map {#sec-derivation-03-04A-source-field-map .unnumbered}

## Purpose

This appendix separates the achieved stationary scalar response from the
provisional directional response.

## Role, regime, and status

- **Role:** weak stationary field construction.
- **Regime:** linear response on the asymptotically flat stationary stage.
- **Status:** scalar Green/Poisson map achieved within the adopted source
  package; directional map retained as a field-side seed.
- **Non-claim:** the scalar and vector kernels are not derived as projections
  of one displayed elementary action, and the directional source/action/readout
  chain is not closed.

## Source packages

Given SI,

$$
\mathcal M=\frac{\mathcal J_k^++\mathcal J_k^-}{2}=\varrho
\quad\text{for any }k,
$$

$$
\mathcal P_i
=\sum_k(\mathcal J_k^+-\mathcal J_k^-)\,e_{(k)i}=j_i.
$$

The second moment $\mathcal C_{ij}$ remains part of transport accounting but
is not an independent source in the minimal field map below.

## Scalar response

The even package sources the dimensionless scalar depth

$$
\boxed{
\theta_0(\mathbf r)
=\frac{G_N}{c^3}\int
\frac{\mathcal M(\mathbf r')}{|\mathbf r-\mathbf r'|}
\,d^3r'}.
\tag{3.4A.1}
$$

Since $\Delta(1/R)=-4\pi\delta^{(3)}(\mathbf r-\mathbf r')$,

$$
\boxed{
\Delta\theta_0=-\frac{4\pi G_N}{c^3}\mathcal M}.
\tag{3.4A.2}
$$

For cold static matter, $\mathcal M=c\rho$. Defining

$$
U:=-c^2\theta_0
$$

then gives

$$
\Delta U=4\pi G_N\rho.
$$

The selected clock-depth package is

$$
G(\theta_0):=\sqrt{1-2\theta_0}.
\tag{3.4A.3}
$$

Equation (3.4A.3) is an exact definition of that package. It does not turn the
flat Green kernel into a nonlinear or moderate-field spatial theory.

## Directional response seed

The odd source motivates the transverse field-side map

$$
\theta_i^\perp(\mathbf r)
=\frac{G_N}{c^3}\int
\frac{\mathcal P_i^\perp(\mathbf r')}{|\mathbf r-\mathbf r'|}
\,d^3r',
\tag{3.4A.4}
$$

or

$$
\Delta\theta_i^\perp
=-\frac{4\pi G_N}{c^3}\mathcal P_i^\perp,
\qquad
\partial_i\theta_i^\perp=0.
\tag{3.4A.5}
$$

The weak Lense--Thirring endpoint requires a carrier- or observer-facing
directional coefficient of magnitude four relative to this primitive kernel.
That endpoint does not select a healthy sign-bearing action. A positive
one-vector action gives the opposite rotating-source orientation; the tested
constrained repair fits the needed stationary coefficient but leaves its
normalization and causal observer transport undetermined. Equations
(3.4A.4)--(3.4A.5) are therefore retained as a provisional response seed, not a
physical vector closure.

## Two assumptions, not one primitive projection

The scalar map uses an even, direction-blind response postulate. The
directional map uses a separate odd transverse response postulate. Their common
$1/R$ kernel is structurally economical, but the displayed elementary
directional contribution does not derive both sectors. Keeping the assumptions
separate prevents the source grammar from carrying more closure than has been
shown.

## Result

The achieved stationary backbone is

$$
\mathcal M
\longrightarrow\theta_0
\longrightarrow U=-c^2\theta_0,
$$

with the Newtonian Poisson normalization fixed. The odd package supplies a
well-defined transverse PDE target, but its action, observable sign, and
causal observer map remain open.
